provenance.contract: This file ships the CATALOGUE OF FACT TYPES, never anybody's facts. A row here says 'annual income is a thing an organisation has, it is money, it is reviewed when accounts are next due, and a funder asking about it tends to use these words'. It never says what any tenant's income is. That is a claim, it is tenant data, and it arrives from a public register, a document or a person — never from a fixture.
provenance.why_typed: Claims carry a kind rather than being free prose because every consumer has to match a fact to something: a register field to import it, a funder's question to pre-fill it, a review rule to age it. Matching free prose is guesswork, and a wrong auto-filled answer is worse than a blank box.
provenance.question_hints: Whole-word tokens that mean a funder's question is asking for this fact. Matched with word boundaries, never as substrings — the CRM learned that lesson when a lookup for 'SAM' hit 'Samantha'. Add hints when a real form uses wording we miss; never add a token so generic it matches everything.
provenance.register_fields: The per-register source paths live in app/claims/registers.py beside the client that reads them, not here — a JSON fixture is the wrong place for the shape of somebody else's API response.

claim_kinds.label: Registered name
claim_kinds.notes: The name on the register, which is often not the name the organisation trades under. Both matter on a form; this is the one a funder checks.

claim_kinds.label: Company number
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation is registered at Companies House under company number {value}.
claim_kinds.notes: Stable for the life of the company. Long review cycle because it only changes on re-registration.

claim_kinds.label: Charity number
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation is a registered charity, number {value}.
claim_kinds.notes: England and Wales numbers are six or seven digits; Scottish numbers carry an SC prefix and come from OSCR; Northern Irish numbers carry NIC.

claim_kinds.label: Legal form
claim_kinds.notes: Registers return codes rather than prose — the client maps them to plain English before a claim is proposed.

claim_kinds.label: Registration status
claim_kinds.notes: Load-bearing for safety rather than for drafting: a dissolved company and a removed charity both still return full data, so the import gates on this before proposing anything.

claim_kinds.label: Date registered
claim_kinds.notes: Incorporation date for a company, registration date for a charity. Answers 'how long have you been operating', which most forms ask in some form.

claim_kinds.label: Registered office
claim_kinds.notes: Rendered to a single line by the register client. Often not the operating address, and a form asking for one rarely wants the other.

claim_kinds.label: Charitable objects
claim_kinds.notes: Verbatim from the governing document, so it is quotable in a bid without paraphrase — which is what a funder checking eligibility actually wants.

claim_kinds.label: What the organisation does
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation describes its activities as: {value}
claim_kinds.notes: The charity's own description as filed. Useful as raw material for a narrative section, rarely usable verbatim as an answer.

claim_kinds.label: Annual income
claim_kinds.notes: Periodic: the current standing figure carries no period, and a series of prior years may be held alongside it with one row per financial year. Review date comes from the filing calendar, never from review_days — hence null.

claim_kinds.label: Financial year end
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation's financial year ends on {value}.
claim_kinds.notes: Drives the review date of every finance claim, which is why it is imported even though few forms ask for it directly.

claim_kinds.label: Reserves
claim_kinds.notes: No register publishes this — it comes from the accounts in the vault, or a person.

claim_kinds.label: Number of employees
claim_kinds.notes: OSCR's annual return carries staff numbers, which neither Companies House nor the Charity Commission for England and Wales publishes. Everywhere else this comes from the accounts or a person.

claim_kinds.label: People supported
claim_kinds.notes: The archetypal claim the brief was written about: true in March, still asserted in July, eighteen months stale by the time anybody checks. Periodic for exactly that reason.

claim_kinds.label: Trustee
claim_kinds.statement_template: {subject} is a trustee of the organisation.
claim_kinds.notes: One row per trustee, the name in `subject`. We store name, role and appointment date only — never the partial date of birth, nationality or occupation the registers also return. OSCR has published trustee names since 9 March 2026, with an exemption route for trustees at risk, so an absent list is normal and never an error.

claim_kinds.label: Director
claim_kinds.statement_template: {subject} is a director of the organisation.
claim_kinds.notes: For a charitable company the directors ARE the charity trustees, which is the fallback that gives a Scottish charitable company a usable board list from Companies House before OSCR access arrives.

claim_kinds.label: Director identity verification
claim_kinds.notes: ECCTA: every director must have verified identity at Companies House by 18 November 2026; after that an unverified director blocks the confirmation statement and the company commits an offence. The officers API returns identity_verification_details in two shapes — a verified date plus the verifying agent, or a bare completion statement — or not at all, which means not verified. Values always begin 'verified' or 'not yet verified'; the readiness panel keys off that prefix, so the prefix is contract, not copy. Review dates ride the confirmation-statement cycle like the other identity facts.

claim_kinds.label: Confirmation statement due
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation's next confirmation statement is due {value}.
claim_kinds.notes: The filing deadline itself, as a fact. Its review date IS the due date, so it goes stale the day it passes and the sweep surfaces it; a re-import refreshes it from the register once the filing is made. Under ECCTA this is also each existing director's personal identity-verification deadline.

claim_kinds.label: Annual accounts due
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation's next annual accounts are due {value}.
claim_kinds.notes: Same shape as confirmation_statement_due: the review date is the deadline, so a passed filing date surfaces through the ordinary staleness machinery rather than a bespoke alarm.

claim_kinds.label: Accreditation
claim_kinds.notes: Review date comes from expires_on, not review_days — an accreditation is current until its certificate lapses, and that date is the only thing worth reviewing against.

claim_kinds.label: Insurance cover
claim_kinds.notes: Subject names the cover type, value the limit of indemnity, expires_on the renewal date. The claim the brief's digest example warns about: cover that expired in April, asserted in a bid in May.

claim_kinds.label: Policy
claim_kinds.statement_template: The organisation has a {subject} policy, last reviewed {value}.
claim_kinds.notes: The value is the policy's own review date, so a policy overdue for review shows as overdue here without a separate mechanism.

claim_kinds.label: Past contract value
claim_kinds.notes: Present for Tenderhouse, which will lean on it heavily. Harmless in the meantime — a tenant with no bids simply has none.

claim_kinds.label: Case study
claim_kinds.notes: Annual review because a case study does not become false, it becomes old — and a five-year-old example reads as one.
